block.title: The fortress burning behind a fighter flying hard toward camera
block.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, widescreen 16:9 arcade composition, subtle CRT scanline glow; ending scene painted at hi-resolution, maximum inferno, ultra-detailed large-format art with pixel-art texture accents. The citadel falls and the whole sky knows it: filling the entire right two-thirds of the frame, a continent-sized enemy fortress-ship is coming down in fire along its full length — a chain of a hundred simultaneous breaches erupting from its spine in the classic arcade ramp, cream-white cores going to amber petals going to rust smoke, the explosions linking into a single luminous fault line that walks across the hull. Its armor layers peel back like bark from a burning tree, revealing dark girders bending inward as the superstructure begins its slow collapse toward the planet's cloud deck below; towers of ember smoke lean sideways in the slipstream of its fall. In the left third of the frame, small and dead-level with the camera, a steel-blue dart fighter flies directly toward the viewer away from the blaze, canopy catching the firelight so its cyan glass burns turquoise-gold at the edges, twin orange engines stretched thin and bright, wings steady. The contrast is the story: one ship, perfectly composed, outrunning an ending it authored. Firelight does all the grading — the left air is smoky gold, the right horizon eaten. Palette of explosion cream-to-rust over deep navy smoke-shadow with embers floating across the entire frame, lifted deep-navy base, never pure black. No text, no letters, no UI.

Fortress must read as SHIP-mass with towers, not a city: negative bans buildings deliberately.
